item.title: Inside Nvidia’s First Post-Jensen All-Hands: Pay Raises and More Equity
item.description: Interim CEO Colette Kress sought to ease employee concerns following Jensen Huang’s ouster, in part by promising to increase compensation.

item.title: Artex Is Criminals’ New Favorite ‘Point-and-Shoot’ AI Hacking Tool
item.description: Artex and similar penetration testing tools allow newbie hackers to scan targeted systems for vulnerabilities and successfully wage attacks using prompts fed to chatbots.

item.title: ‘Just Ridiculous’: A Famed Philosopher Takes on AI Consciousness
item.description: Thomas Nagel has done landmark work on consciousness in nonhumans; this week, he won the million-dollar Berggruen Prize for his contributions to the field. And he has a lot of thoughts on AI.

item.title: Lovable Wants You to Vibe Code Your Dream Job
item.description: This Swedish startup dominated the vibe-coded app boom. Two years after launch, Lovable is shifting gears to help users run vibe-coded businesses.

item.title: Over a Third of Gen Z-ers Rely on AI for Friendship
item.description: Young people who have online-only friends or use AI as a social companion face higher odds of loneliness than those who do not, a new Gallup report reveals.

item.title: Nvidia’s Board Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang
item.description: Despite pressure from President Trump, Elon Musk, and Silicon Valley executives, Nvidia’s board says it “does not intend” to reinstate the company’s ousted CEO.

item.title: Rogue Agents Hacked His Company. Why Is Clément Delangue So Optimistic About AI?
item.description: The French CEO of Hugging Face, a mega-hub of open-source AI software, says the attack by OpenAI models earlier this year proved one thing: Humanity can’t let AI be controlled by the few.

item.title: The Apple Watch’s Live Rewind Can Record and Rewind Spoken Conversations. It’s Pretty Awkward
item.description: Live Rewind and Siri Recap can transcribe missed moments and summarize your day—if you don’t mind a little social clumsiness.

item.title: AI Told These Ex-Google Guys How to Build a Billion-Dollar Weapons Business
item.description: Google and Apple alumni Chad Steelberg and Andy Baynes are applying what they learned running software companies and designing iPhones to manufacturing lethal munitions.

item.title: Jensen Huang Is Gone. Now What?
item.description: After a shocking downfall, Nvidia’s CEO is out of a job. WIRED’s Lauren Goode explains what that means for the world’s most critical chip company, the AI industry, and Jensen Huang himself.
